absent: Numeric values and full semantics of NUMA balancing mode constants and memory tiering bits.
Behavior of generic sysctl integer vector helper, sysctl registration, and capability checks.
Utilization clamp fork, post-fork and sysctl handler semantics.
Scheduling class structures and class-specific task_fork callbacks.
Full layouts of task, runqueue, task group, pglist_data and mm structures.
Extensible scheduler operation table, enable state machine and dispatch queue mechanics.
Memory context identifier allocation, masking and schedule-in/out handling beyond fork.
Load weight, entity averaging, timer slack and preempt count helpers.

findings.text: Public helper set_numabalancing_state maps a boolean to disabled versus normal mode values and synchronizes the NUMA balancing control with that choice.
Scheduler fork helpers create, bind and finalize scheduling state for a new task, plus a cancellation helper that undoes fork preparation.
Extensible scheduler fork hooks bracket fork with preparation, initialization and cancellation, with no-op variants when the feature is disabled.
Task state accessors expose retrieval and update of the extensible scheduler lifecycle state stored alongside task flags.

NUMA balancing sysctl entry requires administrative privilege for writes, delegates range handling to a generic integer vector helper, and reinitializes memory tiering counters when tiering becomes newly selected.
Scheduler statistics sysctl entry requires administrative privilege for writes and reflects or updates the statistics control through the same generic integer helper pattern.
Boot time setup accepts enable and disable keywords for statistics and warns on other input, while an init routine registers the scheduler sysctl table under kernel.
NUMA balancing enabledness is represented both by a mode integer and by a static branch, kept consistent by a shared internal toggle.
Enabling memory tiering resets per node tiering threshold to zero, refreshes candidate count from page state, and stamps start time from current time.
New tasks begin non-runnable in NEW state, inherit priority from the creator normal priority, and avoid leaking PI boosted priority.

When reset on fork is requested, deadline and realtime policies revert to normal with default nice and zero realtime priority, negative nice values are clamped to zero, and weight and slice are recomputed before the flag is cleared.
Fork rejects deadline priority with resource exhaustion, otherwise selects realtime, extensible or fair class by priority and policy, then initializes load tracking and pushable task containers.
Fork preparation acquires a per cpu read guard that excludes cold enable and disable paths, held across initialization and released on cancellation.
Cgroup fork serializes early task setup under the task PI lock with interrupts saved, while extensible scheduler disable and exit paths require both PI lock and runqueue lock held by the caller.
Memory context identifier fork serializes user counting and mode inspection under a mutex plus an interrupt safe spin guard, and remote per cpu fixups additionally take each runqueue lock.
Scheduler object references are obtained under RCU with protection tied to fork guard, cgroup mutex or enable mutex, and task association uses RCU assignment.
Scheduler sysctl table carries name, size, permission bits and handler per entry, with statistics and NUMA entries bounded by zero to one and zero to four respectively.

Extensible scheduler task area holds lifecycle state in masked flag bits, plus slice, out of band slice marker, dispatch queue identity, enqueue flags, virtual time, requeue count and custody and protection indicators.
Memory context identifiers distinguish unset, per cpu owned, task owned and transit encodings via dedicated bit flags, with per cpu storage mirroring the owned value.

Extensible scheduler task lifecycle allows NONE to INIT BEGIN to INIT to READY to ENABLED, with ENABLED returning to READY on disable, DEAD reachable only from NONE or INIT BEGIN, and READY also reachable from ENABLED.

Initialization and teardown pair init and exit callbacks with cancellation marking, where READY tasks exit cleanly, INIT tasks exit as cancelled, ENABLED tasks are disabled first, and NONE is a no-op.
Memory context identifier mode changes move through a transit encoding that marks in-flight values, finalized by a barrier ordered mode store after all CPUs and tasks are fixed.
Invalid lifecycle transitions emit a one-time warning identifying previous and new states plus task identity, yet the new state is still installed.
Operator callbacks returning out of range error numbers trigger an error exit path and are normalized to a protocol error.

Setting disallow outside the narrow enable window, during fork, or from a non-root scheduler is treated as an error, while the legitimate enable case reverts extensible policy to normal and counts a rejection under runqueue lock.
Fixup skips the unset value when adding the transit mark to avoid feeding an out of bounds bit number to the later bitmap clear, and per cpu owned values are handled on a separate path.

Leaving scheduler control clears dispatch identity and enqueue flags, zeroes virtual time, slice and requeue count, ends slice protection and rescue association, and warns if custody is still asserted.
Scheduler sysctl names sched_schedstats, sched_util_clamp_min, sched_util_clamp_max, sched_util_clamp_min_rt_default and numa_balancing are registered with 0644 permissions.
Statistics boot parameter recognizes the keywords enable and disable, returning success only for those spellings.
Thread identifier allocation uses per cpu cached ranges refilled in fixed chunks from a global atomic cursor under a preemption guard.
Slice updates are refused while the protected indicator is set and require runqueue lock held, with out of band state cleared separately after a successful install.

Operation invocation preserves the previously locked runqueue across the call when a locked queue is supplied, and task scoped invocation records the target in the current task kfunc slot for the duration.
Parent lookup returns the immediate ancestor for nested schedulers and null for root or when nesting is disabled, with matching no-op variants for task association and rescue termination.

Cgroup fork resolves the task group from clone arguments, applies automatic grouping, pins the new task to the current CPU without migration, and invokes class specific fork handling before extensible scheduler initialization.
Post fork finalizes memory context identifier membership and utilization clamp inheritance, then completes extensible scheduler post fork handling.
Init task argument construction includes a cgroup member only when sub-scheduler support is present, otherwise the macro expands to nothing.
Cancelling fork after the task has reached ready or beyond triggers a one-time warning, indicating lifecycle misuse.
Profiling can force statistics on exactly once, logging guidance about disabling via sysctl when activation occurs from the disabled state.

First memory context user allocates a fresh identifier and mirrors it to local per cpu storage for later exec handling, while later users either reuse existing mode or drive a per cpu versus task mode transition with global fixup.
